subject: Designing telemetry semantics before or during implementation — logs, metrics, traces, events, spans, attributes,…

evals.prompt: Define observability-modeling in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the observability-modeling skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind observability-modeling. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "set up Sentry error tracking for this app". Should observability-modeling activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force observability-modeling onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to system-interface-contracts, testing-strategy, error-tracking, performance-engineering, event-contract-design, debugging, semantics, performance-budgets.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "design telemetry for this ingestion pipeline so failures can be diagnosed later". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying observability-modeling.

Place observability-modeling among its adjacent skills (system-interface-contracts, testing-strategy, error-tracking, performance-engineering, event-contract-design, debugging, semantics, performance-budgets). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about observability-modeling and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
